source: Yize Wang CV, July 31, 2026; NVIDIA team transition updated by the owner, October 2026

positions.title: Isaac Applications Team
highlights: Implemented Isaac Lab tutorial scripts demonstrating physics backends and the use of PyTorch and Warp.
Trained Franka and SO101 arms to perform lifting tasks using curriculum-based reinforcement learning with PPO.

positions.title: Automotive Vehicle Department
highlights: Implemented a belief-and-heuristics-based framework to construct robust road topology with temporal-spatial fusion.
Served as a mono-repo code approver, reviewing component PRs and driving design iterations to improve end-to-end behavior.
Owned code quality, overseeing Coverity and coverage checks to ensure compliance with AUTOSAR standards for functional safety.
Improved development efficiency by building debugging tools, sharing best practices, and developing automated workflows.

projects.title: Highway NOA (HNOA)
highlights: Delivered China’s first mapless HNOA on SGMW YunDuo using a TI TDA4VH automotive SoC (32 TOPS) and a 1R7V sensor configuration. Features included automatic activation and escalation, on/off-ramp navigation, intelligent lane selection, overtaking, speed adaptation, and avoidance of diversion areas and static obstacles. Achieved over 85% success in merging into and exiting main roads, serving 2,300 customers across 610,000 km of autonomous driving as of December 2023.
Platformized HNOA across vehicle models from multiple OEMs, supporting different SoC configurations and map providers, including AMap and Tencent Map.

Designed HNOA navigation algorithms that achieved over 98% accuracy for navigation-triggered lane changes using only vehicle navigation information, including maneuvers, distance, suggested lanes, and road classes.

projects.title: City NOA (CNOA)
projects.role: Navigation Algorithm Lead & Project Agile Coach
highlights: Designed and delivered CNOA navigation algorithms, achieving robust urban routing based on multi-hypothesis matching of SD maps and online lane perception. The output was presented as a topological graph indicating lane-level probabilistic connectivity.
Led a 12-member CNOA Scrum team as Scrum Master, responsible for planning, tracking, and verifying Stories and Tasks in Sprints.

projects.title: Memory on Driving (MOD)
highlights: Led MOD integration across Perception, Mapping, Localization, Planning, and HMI teams. Demonstrated memory map building, localization, intersection handling, and computational feasibility, securing approvals from multiple OEMs. MOD was released to users in June 2024.

Developed navigation algorithms using dynamic programming to calculate drivable areas and a greedy algorithm to minimize lane changes. Improved decisions across multiple lane options, reduced trajectory-following behavior, and prevented deviations from memory maps.
Optimized reference lines by fusing memory maps and perceived lane markers with iLQR, handling turns, U-turns, on/off-ramps, diverging and merging lanes, and narrow gaps.

Developed intersection path-planning algorithms using third-order Bézier curve optimization, lane-group combinatorial optimization, and Hybrid A* to generate smooth, collision-free reference lines that respect vehicle kinematics.
Planned 9,625 intersection paths in Shanghai; 99% met the required standards, and the remaining 1% were correctly flagged for review.
Deployed the algorithms to the HD-map labeling production platform, increasing labeling efficiency by over 1,000% and replacing error-prone manual operations.
